name: Vex Nullsound Reactive Club Shell
description: A cropped bomber-cut shell in matte black synthleather threaded throughout with micro-filament LED channels that pulse in direct response to ambient bass frequencies — sub-80Hz triggers deep violet blooms, mid-range produces fractured cyan arcs across the chest and shoulders. Collar and cuffs are trimmed in sound-dampening foam wrapped in mirrored mylar. The back panel features a woven pattern that, under UV, resolves into a stylized frequency map of GLMZ's underground club district, known only to those who've been there. Sized for both human and lightly-geneware'd frames.
functionality: Sound-reactive LED system runs on a micro-battery charged by body movement. Collar foam provides mild hearing protection at high decibels. Seam channels at the upper back accommodate spinal port rigs without snagging.
what_it_says: This person knows where the real parties are and has been there more than once.
worn_by: geneware enthusiasts with bioluminescent skin pairings
story_hooks: The frequency map on the back panel leads to a club that officially closed two years ago — someone's still running events there.
A Tier 4 corporate spy is using a counterfeit version of this jacket to infiltrate the underground music scene looking for a missing biotech engineer.
The LED filaments in a batch of these jackets have been laced with a passive signal harvester — someone is mapping BCI signatures at clubs.
